page: Microsoft Azure L64s_v4 is an Lsv4-family virtual machine configured with 64 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this server features 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The underlying hardware includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

A defining characteristic of the L64s_v4 is its massive local storage capacity, featuring 15,359 GB of NVMe SSD storage. This high-density local storage is paired with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, delivering dedicated CPU allocation without GPU acceleration. The system is designed for high-throughput, low-latency storage operations, making it highly suitable for data-intensive workloads.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core scores and static web serving throughput reaching the top 10% tier. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, placing in the top 25% for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. However, single-core performance is more moderate, as shown by stress-ng single-core results falling into the middle 50% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L64s_v4 offers high resource density by bundling massive NVMe storage directly with a substantial memory footprint, reducing the need for external premium storage attachments. This profile is optimal for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and data-intensive applications requiring rapid local scratch space.
